originalGroup.material:
A picture made from leaves

On Sunday, I ____1____ (collect) fallen leaves in the park with Grandma. We did not pick leaves from the trees. The ones on the ground had many different colours, and we chose a few that were clean and dry.

At home, Grandma asked me ____2____ (make) a picture with them. I wanted to create a bird, but the first arrangement looked more like a boat. We laughed and moved the leaves around before using any glue.

I looked ____3____ (careful) at the shapes. A long leaf could be a tail, while a round one could form part of the body. There was ____4____ orange leaf with a curved edge that became a wing.

After ____5____ (choose) the pieces, we placed them on thick paper. My second bird was ____6____ (big) than the first, so I had to leave more room around it. Grandma reminded me to think about the whole page, not only one wing.

I thanked her ____7____ the help, then wrote the date on the back. The finished picture ____8____ (show) a bird sitting on a branch. It did not look exactly like a real bird, but I liked its autumn colours.

Later, my little brother asked whether he could try. We gave ____9____ (he) a few spare leaves and a fresh page. I looked forward ____10____ seeing what he would make. The same leaf, I discovered, could become part of many different pictures.

originalGroup.material:
Wind made from paper

Our English club made a short radio play last week. It ____1____ (record) in a quiet classroom after lessons. The story took place on a windy night, but we had no real wind in the room.

Our teacher asked us ____2____ (think) about ways to make the sound. One student suggested opening the window. That would also let in traffic noise, so we tried another idea. We moved a large sheet of paper slowly near the microphone.

The first attempt was too loud. We listened to the recording and laughed, then moved the paper ____3____ (far) away than before. The sound became softer and fitted the scene better.

A classmate ____4____ enjoyed acting read the opening lines. The rest of us waited quietly until our parts began. We had to listen as well as speak, because a missed turn could leave a long gap in the story.

After ____5____ (finish), we gave the files clear names instead ____6____ leaving them as a list of numbers. This made it easier for our teacher to find the version we wanted to share.

The play had several ____7____ (voice), but everyone helped with the whole result. I was surprised by how ____8____ (use) one piece of paper could be. It was ____9____ small part of the recording, yet it helped create the night we imagined. We thanked our teacher for giving ____10____ (we) time to try more than one idea.

originalGroup.material:
The wall of small book reviews

At the start of term, our class teacher ____1____ (put) a large sheet of paper on the wall. She invited us to write short notes about books we had enjoyed. Each note needed a title and one reason to try the book.

I first copied a long description from the cover of my novel. The teacher asked whether those were my own words. I decided ____2____ (write) a shorter note about the character I remembered best.

A friend ____3____ liked funny stories read my note and borrowed the book. Later, she added her own response. She liked a different part, so our two notes did not look the same. That made the wall more ____4____ (interest), not less useful.

Before ____5____ (add) a new note, we checked that the book's title was clear. Several ____6____ (child) in another class wanted to use our suggestions too. A title written carelessly could make a good recommendation hard to follow.

We used first names instead ____7____ full personal details. The notes were about reading, not a list of information about every student. Our teacher also reminded us to ask before moving someone else's contribution.

By the end of the month, the wall looked ____8____ (colourful) than it had at the beginning. It had become ____9____ useful place to begin a conversation. The teacher thanked ____10____ (we) for keeping the reasons specific. "A good book" was a start, but explaining what we enjoyed helped another reader choose.
